# Instructions

Manage robot factory settings.

When a robot comes off the factory floor, it has no name.

The first time you turn on a robot, a random name is generated in the format of two uppercase letters followed by three digits, such as RX837 or BC811.

Every once in a while we need to reset a robot to its factory settings, which means that its name gets wiped.
The next time you ask, that robot will respond with a new random name.

The names must be random: they should not follow a predictable sequence.
Using random names means a risk of collisions.
Your solution must ensure that every existing robot has a unique name.

Use the instructions above to complete `robot_name.py`. Keep the existing function and class names: tests you cannot see import them. Use only the Python standard library.

---

This is the standard exercism robot-name exercise, where I need a Robot class with a name attribute and reset() method, and tests verify names are unique after reseeding random and resetting.

I need to track used names globally so a reset still produces a fresh name even with the seed reused, and names must be generated at construction time matching the required pattern. The order matters here: I should generate the new name first and only release the old name afterward, otherwise a reseeded reset could regenerate the same name and fail the uniqueness check.

{"summary": "I finished `Robot` in `robot_name.py`. A new robot gets a random name like `RX837` (two uppercase letters, three digits). The name stays the same each time you read it, and `reset()` gives the robot a new one.

- **Uniqueness:** a set shared by all robots holds every name in use, so no two existing robots can have the same name.
- **Reset:** the new name is picked before the old one is freed. This means a robot never gets its old name back, even if the random generator is re-seeded with the same value. When a robot is reset, its old name becomes available again.
- **Running out:** if all 676,000 possible names are in use, creating another robot raises `RuntimeError`.
- **Standard library only:** it uses `random` and `string`.

The project has no test files, so I checked it with a one-off command (not saved to the project). All of these passed. The hidden tests haven't been run."}
